title: Characterization of the path encoding
statement: For every bit string $x$, the following are equivalent. First, there are $n\in\mathbb N$, an $n\times n$ Boolean adjacency matrix $M$, and vertices $s,t<n$ such that $x$ begins with $n$ pairs $11$, followed by $01$; then each matrix bit is represented by an equal pair of bits, followed by $01$; then the binary expansion of $s$ is represented by equal pairs followed by $01$, and the binary expansion of $t$ follows verbatim and ends the string. In addition, there is a walk from $s$ to $t$ using at most $n$ edges of the graph encoded by $M$. Second, $x$ is of the form consisting of the doubled unary encoding of $n$, followed by the similarly encoded matrix $M$, then the similarly encoded binary expansion of $s$, then that of $t$, and $t$ is reachable from $s$ in the directed graph whose vertices are $0,\ldots,n-1$ and whose edges are the true entries of $M$.
